Current : Under active development. Code for the Current release is in the branch for its major version number (for example, v22.x ). Node.js releases a new major version every 6 months, allowing for breaking changes. This happens in April and October every year. Releases appearing each October have a support life of 8 months. Releases appearing each April convert to LTS (see below) each October.

LTS : Releases that receive Long Term Support, with a focus on stability and security. Every even-numbered major version will become an LTS release. LTS releases receive 12 months of Active LTS support and a further 18 months of Maintenance . LTS release lines have alphabetically-ordered code names, beginning with v4 Argon. There are no breaking changes or feature additions, except in some special circumstances.
: Code from the Current branch built every 24-hours when there are changes. Use with caution.
Current and LTS releases follow . A member of the Release Team each Current and LTS release. For more information, see the .
Binaries, installers, and source tarballs are available at .

The directory is an alias for the latest Current release. The latest- directory is an alias for the latest release from an LTS line. For example, the directory contains the latest Hydrogen (Node.js 18) release.

Each directory and filename includes the version (e.g., ), followed by the UTC date (e.g., for April 24, 2024), and the short commit SHA of the HEAD of the release (e.g., ). For instance, a full directory name might look like .
Documentation for the latest Current release is at . Version-specific documentation is available in each release directory in the subdirectory. Version-specific documentation is also at .
Download directories contain a file with SHA checksums for the files and the releaser PGP signature.
You can get a trusted keyring from nodejs/release-keys, e.g. using :
Alternatively, you can import the releaser keys in your default keyring, see for commands on how to do that.
Then, you can verify the files you've downloaded locally (if you're using your default keyring, pass ):
curl -fsO \ gpgv --keyring= --output SHASUMS256.txt SHASUMS256.txt.asc \ shasum --check SHASUMS256.txt --ignore-missing
